summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of recurrent left lower extremity cellulitis, chronic venous stasis, lipodermatosclerosis, bioprosthetic aortic valve, pacemaker, and heart failure was admitted for worsening left leg pain, erythema, and swelling unresponsive to outpatient oral antibiotics. She presented with a low-grade fever and a history of recent watery diarrhea. In the ED, she received IV vancomycin and ceftriaxone, and imaging ruled out DVT but confirmed significant subcutaneous edema. During her hospital stay, she improved clinically with IV antibiotics, and a PICC line was placed for outpatient continuation of vancomycin. Her acute kidney injury, attributed to volume depletion while on torsemide, resolved with IV fluids, and the diuretic was held at discharge. She was discharged home with instructions to complete a 10-day IV antibiotic course, hold torsemide and potassium until follow-up, and monitor for recurrence of infection.
